name: a-disposable-film-seaside
prompt: A real holiday snapshot from about 1998, scanned from a glossy six-by-four print that came back from the chemist in a paper wallet, taken on a cheap plastic throwaway film camera by someone's mum. A blustery midday on an English pebble beach: in the middle, a cheerful sunburnt grandad in a short-sleeved shirt and grey trousers rolled to the knee, bare feet on the stones, hoists a soft-serve vanilla cone high above his head like a cup he has just won, a drip of melting ice cream running down his wrist, grinning with his eyes screwed up against the wind. Around him two small kids in bright cagoules and shorts clutch plastic buckets and spades, one shrieking with laughter, a nan in a folding chair behind them with her cardigan blowing open. A row of faded red-white-and-blue striped canvas windbreaks flaps behind the family, wooden poles hammered into the shingle, a grey-green choppy sea and a pale washed-out sky beyond. Shot at standing height with a fixed wide plastic lens, the horizon tilted a few degrees, the framing a little careless, the soft pinkish blur of a fingertip creeping into the bottom corner. Harsh flat overhead sun, slightly overexposed so the sky is nearly white and the highlights bloom, faces lifted and warm with a yellow-orange cast, the sky and sea leaning cool cyan, shadows a bit muddy and greenish. Soft focus that is never quite sharp, low contrast, coarse visible film grain, corners noticeably darkened, faint colour fringing at the edges. Unposed, mid-laugh, honest and a bit imperfect, the kind of picture that ends up in a family album. No text, no date stamp, no logos or lettering anywhere. Thanks.
